rationale.text: The test has one requirement: with the four spacing changes applied together, text stays readable. The four lines are the conditions of the display change, not separate demands, and the methodology applies all four at once with fixed values (line-height 1.5 on every element, margin-bottom 2em on p elements, letter-spacing 0.12em and word-spacing 0.16em on every element), then checks each passage of text. The particular cases exempt content the user cannot restyle: captions burned into a video, images of text, and text inside a canvas element. Readable is judgment in general: text that spills over other content, moves out of view or is truncated with an ellipsis may or may not stay readable. The candidate is none. The custom check applies the methodology's values and looks for a character that was inside the padding box of an ancestor whose overflow is hidden before the change and lies outside it after. Its fault is evidence only, because lying outside that padding box does not prove the character is cut off. An absolutely positioned descendant whose containing block lies outside the overflow:hidden ancestor is not clipped by it (CSS 2.2, overflow clipping). Codex showed this in a browser: a relatively positioned outer block, a static 68 px inner block with overflow hidden, and an absolutely positioned span inside it whose offset parent is the outer block; after the spacing change the last character of the word lay wholly outside the inner block's padding box, yet it stayed painted and readable, and hit testing still found the span. The check's predicate held and its fault would have been false. The check also does not verify that readable content was actually lost, nor that the margin values won the cascade everywhere it compares. The link keeps its routes and its partial scope and becomes evidence_only. What would raise the entry: a check that establishes the real clipping chain for the text (the clipping ancestor lies on the text's containing-block chain, with no positioned escape), verifies that the cut-off content is lost to the reader, and verifies that every prescribed value took effect, with fixtures for this positioned case, a genuinely clipped in-flow span and a clipped region with a working reveal control. No axe rule is tagged for this test. Applicability is judgment: a page whose only text is in images, burned-in captions or canvas would make the test not applicable, and telling text in an image from other images is judgment. Needs is empty: the check changes the styles itself on the page as loaded, which needs no user interaction.
